Playbook.name: QA - Matched Clear Text Protocols - Firewalls - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: Traffic on clear-text protocol ports (FTP 21, Telnet 23, SMTP 25, POP/IMAP, SNMP, MSSQL 1521, etc.) crossing a security boundary was observed, excluding intra-RFC1918 and Microsoft destinations. Triage question: is a sensitive protocol exposed in clear text (a hygiene/exposure risk), or expected legacy traffic?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Cleartext protocols expose credentials and data to interception; in a bank this is a compliance and credential-theft risk more than an active attack.

Assets.AssetType: FortiGate perimeter and internal firewalls (HQ + DR)
Internal server and user segments behind the FortiGate

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: FortiGate logs shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-fortinet_fortigate.* (verified live).

Fields: fortinet.firewall.subtype (ips/dns/...), fortinet.firewall.action, fortinet.firewall.severity, fortinet.firewall.attack, fortinet.firewall.srccountry/dstcountry ('Reserved' = RFC1918 internal), fortinet.firewall.cfgpath, dns.question.name, source.ip, destination.ip, destination.port.

Signal.Name: Cleartext protocol crossing boundary
Signal.Details: dst_port in the cleartext set, not intra-internal, not Microsoft.

Input.name: $source_ip
Input.description: Source of the cleartext traffic (if the alert scopes one).

InitialAssessment.Rule: This is primarily a hygiene finding; escalate only if the cleartext traffic carries credentials to/from an untrusted network or a sensitive system.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether cleartext protocol usage represents a real exposure (sensitive system / untrusted path) or expected legacy internal traffic.

Step.name: Cleartext connections: protocol, endpoints, direction
Step.Purpose: Identify which cleartext protocols, between which endpoints, and whether the path crosses a trust boundary.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.traffic-* | WHERE destination.port IN (20, 21, 23, 25, 110, 143, 161, 1521) AND fortinet.firewall.action == "accept" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS conns = COUNT(*), sources = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.ip), dcountry = VALUES(fortinet.firewall.dstcountry) BY destination.port, destination.ip | SORT conns DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Telnet(23)/FTP(21) to a sensitive host, or any cleartext to/from an external destination (dcountry not Reserved), is the real exposure. Intra-internal legacy app traffic is lower risk.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows cleartext protocol traffic crossing to/from an EXTERNAL destination (credentials exposed over untrusted path).
Node.Result: True Positive (Cleartext Exposure - remediate, escalate to security engineering)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows cleartext to a sensitive internal system (DB/admin) that should use encrypted protocols.
INV-01 shows expected legacy internal application traffic with a documented exception.
Cleartext usage whose sensitivity/path cannot be determined.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-FGCLEAR-CONN to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Expected legacy internal application traffic on a cleartext protocol with a documented exception.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the documented exception; close as benign_activity/accepted_risk.

TruePositive.Definition: Cleartext exposure of credentials/data over an untrusted path.

Indicators.Item: No encryption where it is required.

SOCAction.Item: Remediate: move to an encrypted protocol; restrict the exposure.
Escalate to security engineering; assess credential exposure.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A sensitive system misconfigured to use an insecure protocol.

SOCAction.Item: Reconfigure the system for encrypted transport; document remediation.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: For external exposure: remediate the path promptly.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Migrate cleartext protocols to encrypted equivalents; restrict where legacy is unavoidable.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Inventory and eliminate cleartext protocols on sensitive systems; enforce encryption policy.

QualityChecks.Check: Converted from the QA ES|QL rule; this is hygiene, best run as a periodic report rather than a real-time alert.
AcceptRisk applies where legacy cleartext is documented and time-boxed.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Documented legacy exception confirmed; risk accepted with expiry.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Cleartext exposure remediated or migrated to encrypted transport.
